text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a regression in nightly (packing-fit allocator landing) on long-context tests. Memory spikes and a couple of OOMs when we run 40k+ seq workloads, even though avg batch sizes are small. attaching short profile summary below.

tyler: ah, which profile? kernel chooser or allocator traces?

maria: allocator + kernel-chooser traces. quick repro we used: 
```
# repro command we used
python -m tools.microbench --model=gpt-neox --seq=40960 --batch=1 --pad=dynamic
# truncated output
alloc_peak: 13.4GB
ffn_workspace_peak: 2.2GB (observed FlashAttention->Triton fallback at seq=2048)
kv_cache_frag: 12.3%
kernel_choice: flashattn v2 -> triton_fallback (latency bump + extra workspace alloc)
```

cheng: 12% kv frag sounds like our per-request variable-length KV allocations are leaving lots of holes. packing-fit change could increase internal fragmentation if align/granularity increased.

olivia: also worth noting FlashAttention picks different kernel when padded_seq aligns differently. If padding takes you above some lane boundary it picks a triton kernel that needs a separate large workspace.

samir: do we know the pad thresholds? IIRC flashatten kernel selection was tuned to multiples of 16/32 tokens + warp-friendly sizes; Triton fallback when blocked threads > X or smem exceed threshold.

maria: yes — from the trace: at pad=2048 we flip. microtrace shows kernel chooser flag `lane_align=32` and `shared_mem_limit=65536`. When packing-fit rounded a lot of small KV buffers up to 128KB chunks, total gmem usage moved us past the chooser boundary.

tyler: rough theory: packing-fit allocator switches from best-fit->first-fit-like behavior for speed, so it coalesces adjacent small frees into the first hole that fits, but also enforces a 128KB alignment for returned chunks. That alignment increases fragmentation for KV cache entries which are many small objects.

cheng: options: 1) reduce chunk alignment for small allocs to 4KB/8KB 2) keep packing-fit for large allocations only (FFN workspaces) 3) adopt a separate KV suballocator optimized for small variable-length buffers (slab or bucket)

olivia: we should also consider batch-alignment heuristics: if we nudge batching to align sequence lengths to the FlashAttention sweet spot (pad-to-16/32 token buckets) we avoid triton fallback. Could be an orthogonal fix.

maria: ran two quick experiments:
- experiment A: packing-fit with 8KB min-align for small allocs -> peak alloc dropped 9%, kv_frag down to 6.1%, no kernel flip in 10 runs.
- experiment B: revert to previous allocator -> stable but slower allocation latency, no regression.

samir: nice. can you paste the small bench output?

maria: pasted below: 
```
# experiment A
alloc_peak: 12.2GB
ffn_workspace_peak: 2.0GB
kv_cache_frag: 6.1%
throughput: 98 seq/s

# experiment B (legacy)
alloc_peak: 12.0GB
ffn_workspace_peak: 1.9GB
kv_cache_frag: 4.8%
throughput: 100 seq/s
```

tyler: interesting tradeoff: legacy has slightly better frag and throughput but packing-fit was introduced for allocation latency improvements under high-concurrency. Maybe we can do hybrid: packing-fit only for >1MB allocations and small slab for <1MB.

cheng: agree. propose: implement KV slab allocator with bucket sizes [1KB,4KB,16KB,64KB,256KB], ensure 4KB alignment, and keep packing-fit for >512KB. That should minimize fragmentation and preserve speed for big workspaces.

olivia: and on batching side: add an opt-in route config `pad_to_flash_alignment: true` which will pad short requests from customers that opt into lower latency/cost. In practice it nudges batch padding to the nearest 16/32 multiple.

tyler: small nit: need to ensure padding doesn't blow cost for very short requests; make it a heuristic: only pad up to N tokens if expected reduce kernel flips. we can collect prediction from kernel-chooser profiler.

infra-bot: perf-job queued: run/ws-packing-fit/2356789012/bench-40k-seq with both allocator variants (A/B) nightly x10 runs.

maria: action items I can take this week:
- implement KV slab prototype and run microbench (owner: maria)
- add metric for "kernel flip events" to trace pipeline (owner: tyler)
- add batch alignment opt-in flag to routes (owner: olivia)
- schedule canary on Dedicated to validate before full rollout (owner: samir)

samir: timeline?

maria: prototype + microbench by Thu, rollout plan Friday. will post results here.

tyler: I'll wire the kernel-flip metric into console (per-route) and add alert if flips > 1% of requests in 10m.

cheng: one more thing — consider reclaim-on-idle for KV: if request distribution has long tails we can age small KV slabs and coalesce during low load windows. reduces steady-state frag.

maria: yep will add age-based coalesce to prototype (toggleable).

olivia: cheers. please include the microbench script + seed config so QE can reproduce.

maria: will do. throwing the initial patch into `eng-runtime/allocator/pack-fit-kv-slab` branch and link when ready. :+1:

samir: thanks — nice diagnostic. small follow-up: capture a kernel-chooser trace for the exact run that OOMed and attach. we need the full stack (allocator snapshot + kernel choice) to avoid flip-chasing later.

maria: yes will attach the trace to the perf-job once collected.

olivia: if anyone wants to pair on the slab design I'm free after 2pm.

cheng: ping me, i'll join.

maria: thanks all, will update here with bench artifacts.
